columns.description: The policy product code for the version, such as MOTOR_COMP.
The rule used to resolve the customer record from duplicate CRM entries.
The confidence score for the customer record resolution, with 1.0 indicating the highest confidence.
Unique SHA-256 hash of the uploaded document file.
Number of pages in the document.
Timestamp when the document was registered in the system.
Reference to the prior document version that this upload replaces.
The document type for the chunk, such as FIR or INVOICE.
The source file name for the document version that the chunk came from.
The version number of the document file represented by the chunk.
The shop's address as recorded in the garage registry.
The shop's phone number in E.164 format.
The shop's network membership status, such as empanelled.
The dataset where the held record belongs.
The key or identifier of the record held at the quality gate.
The quality rule that caused the record to be held.
The message explaining why the record was held.
The current quality-gate status of the record.
The timestamp when the quality issue was detected.
Unique identifier for each entity mention record.
Type of entity referenced by the mention, such as claim, person, phone, repair shop, or vehicle.
Raw text captured for the entity mention as it appears in the source.
Source system or document set where the mention was found.
Pointer to the specific record or document location for the mention.
Claim identifier associated with the mention.
Page number where the mention appears in a document, when available.
Text chunk identifier where the mention appears, when available.
How the mention was captured, such as from a record or a document page.
Hint indicating a possible GSTIN related to the mention, when available.
Hint indicating a possible customer related to the mention, when available.
Unique identifier for the mention being resolved.
Identifier of the resolved entity for the mention.
Resolution rule used to map the mention to the entity.
Confidence score for the entity resolution.
Count of claims in the past 30 days that share a contact with this claim.
Count of claims in the past 30 days associated with the same repair shop as this claim.
Indicator that the contact phone number does not belong to the claimant.
Timestamp when these claim features were computed.
The fraud model version used to generate the claim signal values.
The date and time until which the versioned claim signals remain valid.
The input features and values used to compute the claim signals.
Insurance segment used to group settled claims for the benchmark distribution.
Type of loss used to group settled claims, such as collision or flood.
Severity band used to group settled claims into comparable claim size ranges.
Number of settled claims included in the benchmark calculation for the group.
10th percentile of approved settlement amounts for the group.
Median approved settlement amount for the group.
90th percentile of approved settlement amounts for the group.
Timestamp when these benchmark values were computed.
SHA-256 hash identifying the uploaded document's file content.
Number of pages in the uploaded document.
Date and time when the document was registered in the document register.
Reference to the earlier document version that this document supersedes, when applicable.
Identifies the dataset containing the record that was held for a quality issue.
Identifies the specific record that was held for review.
States the data quality rule that the record failed.
Provides additional information about the quality issue detected for the record.
Shows the current quality-gate disposition of the record, such as held.
Records when the quality issue was detected and the record was held.
Number of other claims in the previous 30 days that share a contact with this claim.
Number of claims associated with the same shop in the previous 30 days.
Indicator showing whether the contact phone number differs from the claimant’s phone number.
Timestamp when the claim features were computed.
Identifies the fraud model and version used to compute the claim signals.
Specifies the date and time through which the claim signals remain valid.
Stores the feature values used to compute the claim signals, including recent claim activity, contact details, policy changes, and policy age.
Segment used to group settled claims in the benchmark.
Loss type used to group settled claims in the benchmark.
Severity band used to group settled claims in the benchmark.
Number of settled claims included in the benchmark group.
10th percentile of approved settlement amounts for the benchmark group.
50th percentile, or median, of approved settlement amounts for the benchmark group.
90th percentile of approved settlement amounts for the benchmark group.
Timestamp when the benchmark statistics were computed.
SHA-256 hash identifying the uploaded document's file content.
Number of pages in the uploaded document.
Date and time when the document was registered in the platform.
Reference to the earlier document version that this document replaces, when applicable.
Identifies the dataset containing the record held by the quality gate.
Identifies the specific record held by the quality gate.
States the data quality rule that caused the record to be held.
Provides additional information about the quality issue identified for the record.
Shows the current quality-gate status of the record.
Records the timestamp when the quality issue was detected.
Number of other claims in the 30-day period that share a contact with this claim.
Number of claims associated with the same shop in the 30-day period.
Indicator that the contact phone number does not match the claimant's phone number.
Timestamp when the claim features were computed.
Identifies the version of the model used to calculate the claim signals.
Shows the date and time through which the claim signals are valid.
Contains the input feature values used to calculate the claim signals.
Business segment associated with the settled claims included in the benchmark.
Type of loss associated with the settled claims included in the benchmark.
Severity category assigned to the settled claims included in the benchmark.
Number of settled claims used to calculate the amount distribution for the segment, loss type, and severity band.
10th percentile of approved settlement amounts for the segment, loss type, and severity band.
50th percentile, or median, of approved settlement amounts for the segment, loss type, and severity band.
90th percentile of approved settlement amounts for the segment, loss type, and severity band.
Timestamp when the benchmark statistics were calculated.
